LESSON: SILENT READING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: READING
Topic 3.3: Silent reading

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Silent reading. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: When do we read learner should be able to: silent reading skills for efficient silently?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons
2. read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups
3. answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SILENT READING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Silent reading helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SILENT READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons

What this means
In this part you learn to read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Silent reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups

What this means
In this part you learn to read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Silent reading to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent

What this means
In this part you learn to answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Silent reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Silent reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Silent reading to a partner. (skill: read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Silent reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons.
3. Practise this skill: read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups.
4. Practise this skill: answer comprehension questions  Learner should be provided with from texts read follow-up activities for sustained silent.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Silent reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Silent reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Silent reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. When do we read learner should be able to: silent reading skills for efficient silently?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Silent reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: read texts and passages silently reading(through guiding questions, 3 lessons.
5. Be able to: read silently showing sustained timing reading) focus for longer periods (15-20  Learners discuss questions after silent minutes) reading in pairs and groups.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
